_why: od9 does not use the ecosystem's crons/ convention — its scheduled scripts live under api/drip/, which is why this linter reported 'scanned 0 cron(s) — CLEAN' for the whole time it existed. A gate reading a directory this repo does not have is green for the wrong reason.
_duplicate_sender_finding: api/drip/processor.php and api/drip/sender.php are two implementations of the SAME job — both select due enrollments, send, log to od9_drip_log and advance the step. Only sender.php is scheduled. The choice was made against the LIVE SCHEMA, not by recency: processor.php's query names four columns that do not exist (e.id, e.sequence_id, s.id, st.id; the real ones are enrollment_id, sequence_name, sequence_id, step_id), so it dies on its first statement. It was briefly scheduled on 2026-09-01 and logged exactly that, which is how this was caught — note it is also the file the 206acb6 fix touched, so 'most recently maintained' was the wrong signal and nearly the wrong answer. Retiring processor.php is a repo decision left to the owner. NOTE for schema-usage-lint: these are WHERE/JOIN phantoms, the blind spot already recorded as its next gate.
_extra_cron_globs_note: Listed one by one rather than as api/drip/*.php on purpose. That directory also holds webhook.php, which is a WEB endpoint reached by Square and Discord and must not have a CLI guard, and webhook_secret.config.php, which is configuration. Globbing the directory would flag both for 'no CLI guard' — a false positive on the very first run is how a gate loses its audience. These four are the scheduled ones; each already opens with php_sapi_name() !== 'cli'.
_crontab_note: tools/crontab.offda9.txt is now committed, so the cross-reference against prod's real schedule runs here — the check that caught cred-drift-monitor running repo-orphaned for 7 weeks. It reads every crontab line whose script path starts with the prefix and asserts the repo actually contains that file, which is what turns 'the crontab and the repo agree' from an assumption into a per-deploy claim. The earlier note said committing this file was the obvious next improvement; scheduling the drip on 2026-09-01 made it possible, because until then offda9 had no crontab at all.
